threads.body: `error.type` is typically a string-valued attribute in common telemetry conventions, while `rpc.response.status_code` here describes a numeric JSON-RPC error code. Saying they “have the same value” is ambiguous/possibly incorrect across types. Please clarify whether `error.type` should record the numeric code as a string (e.g., \"-32601\"), or define a stable string mapping (e.g., \"jsonrpc.-32601\" / \"Method not found\") so producers/consumers can rely on a consistent representation.

threads.body:
The first paragraph of this note already states both facts: `error.type` takes the string representation of a qualifying JSON-RPC error code, and it is set for failures with no error response. Restating them here under a different condition, "indicates an operation failure" rather than "classifies as an error", leaves the reader to work out whether the two conditions mean the same thing. Only the comparison with `rpc.response.status_code` is new, and that is what #313 asks for.

```suggestion
          `rpc.response.status_code` carries the same string representation of
          the JSON-RPC error code. Unlike `rpc.response.status_code`,
          `error.type` is also set when no JSON-RPC error response is available.
```
